title: Proximity-based column visibility + ARIA announcements for virtualized tables
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Large, virtualized tables overwhelm narrow viewports on small screens and in embedded panels. Users frequently lose context when multiple low-priority columns push important columns offscreen. Existing density modes compress spacing but don't change visibility, and current keyboard/nav behavior is brittle when columns are programmatically collapsed.

Proposal: Introduce a proximity-based column visibility layer that temporarily collapses low-priority columns that are distant from the user's current horizontal viewport (or focus). This is different from static collapse presets: columns are hidden based on viewport proximity and user focus, then smoothly expanded on hover, keyboard focus, or when sorting/filtering affects the column. Add ARIA live-region announcements and explicit focus handling so screen-reader users are informed when columns collapse/expand.

Goals: reduce horizontal scroll friction, preserve discoverability, maintain keyboard-first accessibility, keep density tokens consistent, and minimize layout jumps for virtualized rendering.
acceptance_criteria: When the table is wide and virtualized, low-priority columns outside a configurable proximity threshold are collapsed into a compact pill that shows the column label and a count of hidden cells.
Hover or focus on a collapsed pill expands the column inline without a full re-layout and retains virtualization performance (no frame drops on 100k-row tables).
ARIA live region announces collapses/expansions with concise messages (e.g., '3 columns collapsed to conserve space; press Enter to expand').

Keyboard navigation respects collapsed state: Tab/Arrow navigation moves into expanded content predictably; pressing Enter or Space on pill expands it and moves focus to the first cell of that column.

Density tokens (compact/comfortable) map to proximity thresholds and collapsed-pill styling, and tokens are defined in the design system tokens file with clear tokens for spacing, pill radius, and micro-interaction durations.
Design updated in Figma, and a prototype exists demonstrating mouse, keyboard, and screen-reader flows. Design review signed off by Accessibility lead.
Engineering implements RTL-safe collapsing and integrates with existing virtualization overscan logic; perf regression <10% on p75 render time compared to current baseline.
design_notes: Introduce a new token group: token.table.proximity.thresholds (small|medium|large) mapped to px values for each density mode.
Collapsed pill UI uses token.color.surface-muted for background and token.typography.micro for label; include subtle hairline separator for multi-column pills.
Micro-interaction: expand/collapse should use 120ms opacity + 160ms translate easing to feel responsive without jank.
Visual affordance: a small chevron icon indicates expandable content; when multiple columns collapsed, show first column label + '+N' suffix.
Edge case: when a sort/filter action targets a collapsed column, auto-expand that column and announce change to screen reader.
engineering_considerations: Tie proximity calculation to current horizontal scroll position and active focus cell; compute which columns are within threshold per render tick (debounced at 50ms).
Avoid full DOM reflow: render collapsed columns as a single virtual column node that expands into real column cells on demand; reuse KV cache where possible.
Integrate with existing column-resize handles: when a collapsed column is resized, uncollapse it and persist user preference in local layout state.
Overscan: ensure virtualization overscan still fetches rows for expanded state; prefetch cells for up to 1 collapsed pill expansion to keep perceived latency low.
Accessibility: implement aria-live polite region for status messages and ensure screen-reader focus is preserved when columns collapse/expand.
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Initial triage — flagged as high impact for embedded console workflows. Drafted token recommendations and three visual variations (stacked pill, inline cropped, and overlay expansion).

2026-03-11 Evan Patel: Engineering sync — feasibility looks good. Concern about reflow on expand for very wide columns; will prototype a single-node expansion approach to avoid DOM churn. Assigned ENG-4210 to spike performance impact.

2026-03-11 Priya Rao (Accessibility): Reviewed flows. Request: ARIA announcements must be concise and actionable; add guidance for NVDA/VoiceOver quirks. Suggested adding e2e screen-reader checks in QA.
2026-03-12 Liam O'Connor (PM): Approved scope for Cycle 2026-W11; asked that we include metric hooks for horizontal scroll reduction and focus-loss incidents. Will add to product analytics dashboard.

2026-03-12 Maya Chen: Updated Figma with keyboard-first prototype and micro-interaction timings. Pushed an updated spec link in this ticket. Next: handoff to ENG spike, accessibility checklist, and QA test plan.
